clue.text: Does he really bully his secretary?

definitions.text: Does he really bully his secretary?

parts.words: Does he really bully his secretary?
parts.note: a boss who reads letters out to a secretary for typing does this, and the clue asks whether such a boss is also a tyrant

explanation.surface: A question about whether a boss mistreats an office assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is the verb hidden in the title: a man who dictates to his secretary is, in one sense, a dictator, whether or not he is a tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler is a tyrant, and the word also describes anyone who dictates letters.

clue.text: Ruin a European party

parts.note: un is the French for 'a', so 'a' in a European language
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Someone wrecks a gathering held by a continental.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo plans or a person is to bring them to ruin, as in 'his pride undid him'.

clue.text: The drink's added to, getting mellow

parts.note: 'the drink' is slang for the sea, so 'the drink's' gives SEA'S
on means added to, as in 'tack this on'

explanation.surface: A drink is topped up and the drinker grows mellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' joins the wordplay to the definition. 'The drink' means the sea, not a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber or wine left to mature is seasoned, so to season is to mellow with time.

clue.text: Group has nothing after short tour

indicators.note: after means the zero comes behind the shortened tour
short means the word for a tour loses its final letter

parts.note: a trip is a tour or journey
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A band has no bookings after cutting its tour short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes the last letter of the tour word; 'has' is a link, and the surface's band on tour is a misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A threesome of players or singers is a small musical group.

clue.text: To improve morale, I cooked and had a meal

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of morale and I are worked over into a new arrangement

parts.note: ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: A cook boosts the team's spirits by preparing and eating a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' is the anagram signal, not part of the meal; 'had a meal' supplies the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Ameliorate is a formal verb for making something better.

clue.text: Run south with one in arduous journey

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south

indicators.note: in puts the letter for one inside the word for an arduous journey

parts.note: a trek is a long hard journey
A, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A hiker heads south with a companion on a hard trek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins S to TREAK (A inside TREK).
explanation.definitionFit: A run of wins or losses is called a streak.

clue.text: Top clan regathering in wood

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged clan inside the word for a kind of wood

parts.note: pine is a common wood

indicators.note: regathering suggests the letters of clan gather again in a new order

explanation.surface: A Scottish clan reassembles in a forest at the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regathering' shuffles the clan's letters, which then sit inside the tree; 'Top' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point or peak of something is its top.

clue.text: Just the thing for exploring Mars?

definitions.text: Just the thing for exploring Mars?

parts.words: Just the thing for exploring Mars?
parts.note: the famous 'canals' once claimed to be seen on Mars would need a narrow inland waterway vessel

explanation.surface: A question about the right vehicle for a mission to the red planet.
explanation.walkthrough: Nineteenth-century astronomers thought they saw canals on Mars; a narrowboat built for canals would suit them.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow barge built for inland waterways would suit the supposed channels on the planet.

clue.text: Ancient measure stored in memory

indicators.note: stored in puts the printing measure inside the word for memory

parts.note: learning by rote is learning by memory
an em is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: An old unit of length is kept in someone's memory.
explanation.walkthrough: The em is a printer's unit of width, a convention worth knowing; 'Ancient' means far back in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote can mean far back in time, as in 'the remote past'.

clue.text: It's sharp? Ultimately flat on instrument

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word flat

parts.note: a horn is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A musician hears a note that is sharp, then one flat, on a horn.
explanation.walkthrough: Sharp and flat look musical; 'sharp' is part of the definition and 'flat' only gives its last letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickle on a rose stem is pointed enough to pierce skin.

clue.text: Assume it has a blade

explanation.surface: Something takes a role and carries a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a burden is to assume it; the shoulder joint carries the bone called the scapula, or shoulder blade.

clue.text: Dropping into second tenement produces a snag

indicators.note: into puts the word for dropping inside the second-plus-tenement pair

parts.note: a tenement is a block of flats
tumbling means falling or dropping

explanation.surface: Something falls into a second apartment building, causing a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' splits the second-plus-tenement pair around the falling word; 'produces' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle that trips progress is a hitch or problem.

clue.text: Slip to Rome, baroque city

indicators.note: baroque means extravagantly ornate, hinting the letters of slip to Rome are twisted into a new shape

explanation.surface: A traveller heads to Rome, a city famed for baroque architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baroque' rearranges the ten letters of SLIP TO ROME.
explanation.definitionFit: A metropolis is a very large and important city.

clue.text: Given the chop frequently?

parts.note: read 'the chop' as a cut of meat: something a meat trader hands over to customers again and again

explanation.surface: Someone keeps getting fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given the chop' looks like sacked; read literally, a butcher gives out chops all day, and the answer also means hacked to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacked up or slaughtered describes something chopped crudely, like meat in a shop.

clue.text: Budget speech gives nothing away

indicators.note: gives away means the zero letter is taken out of the word for a speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Chancellor's Budget speech reveals nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives ... away' drops O from ORATION. The Budget is the UK's annual financial statement.
explanation.definitionFit: To ration supplies is to budget them, allowing a fixed amount each.

clue.text: Drinking aids desperate people grasp?

explanation.surface: Thirsty, desperate people reach for something to drink with.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin tubes for sipping drinks; and desperate people 'clutch at' these flimsy stalks in the idiom.

clue.text: I advanced in shady cover, without a sound

indicators.note: cover means the word for shady wraps round I and the word for advanced

parts.note: sly means sneaky or shady
lent means advanced, as of money

explanation.surface: Someone moves forward quietly under shady cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in shady cover' wraps the sneaky word round I and the loan word; 'advanced' means lent money, not moved forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something noiselessly means making no noise at all.

clue.text: Like taking a dim view of things, in a way

definitions.text: Like taking a dim view of things, in a way

parts.words: Like taking a dim view of things, in a way
parts.note: taking a dim view means disapproving, but read literally it is seeing things blurred, as someone with poor distance vision does

explanation.surface: Someone disapproves of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking a dim view' is an idiom for disapproving; read literally it means seeing things blurred, which is how myopic people see, and also lacking foresight.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopically, or without thinking ahead, describes how someone with poor distance sight looks at things.

clue.text: Set day arranged, regular date

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of set day are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A fixed day is arranged for a recurring appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set day' and 'date' look like a calendar; the date is a romantic partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend, someone you go out with consistently.

clue.text: Cut from design — or excise

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words design, or, excise

explanation.surface: Something is removed from a design or cut out.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across desIGN OR Excise. 'Cut' means snub, not slice.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to snub or pointedly disregard them.

clue.text: Passion for Ovid, note, in translation

indicators.note: in translation means the letters of Ovid and note are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A reader's love of the Roman poet Ovid, noted in a translation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in translation' rearranges OVID and NOTE; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent love or deep dedication to someone is a passion.

clue.text: I paid up for article

indicators.note: up means the word for paid is read from the bottom in this down light

parts.note: met means paid, as in 'met the bill'

explanation.surface: Someone settles the bill for an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MET to TEM in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single thing or article in a list.

clue.text: Mellow in American State prison

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
pen is slang for penitentiary, a prison

explanation.surface: Someone softens while in an American state jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that matures grows soft and sweet, as wine mellows.

clue.text: Agreement in case, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for 'in case' is heard, not seen

parts.note: packed means put in a case or suitcase

explanation.surface: An accord is reached in a legal case, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in case' looks legal; it means packed in a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal deal or treaty.

clue.text: Counsel and DA looking back on crime

indicators.note: looking back means the letters D and A are read in reverse

parts.note: vice is crime or wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A lawyer and a District Attorney review an old crime.
explanation.walkthrough: DA is a US District Attorney; 'looking back' turns those two letters round, with 'on' as a link before the crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel is guidance or recommendation given to someone.

clue.text: Guy's right: I twice clued ineptly

indicators.note: ineptly means the letters of I, I and clued are clumsily arranged
twice means I is taken two times

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that he wrote two awkward clues.
explanation.walkthrough: To guy someone is to mock them; R follows, with I twice and CLUED mixed by 'ineptly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is an old verb meaning to mock or poke fun at them.
